mechanisms.behavior: One-ball outhole returns a drained ball to the manual shooter. Public8 with lamp34=0 ejects it; the same public address with lamp34=1 ejects the saucer. The ball stack is table routing, not a measured extra trough assembly. Drain collection does not directly actuate the outhole contact. Shared public-driver ownership is recorded once under mechanism.expander; the exact selected loads are stated here and in its relay relationships.
mechanisms.label: Outhole and Manual Shooter

mechanisms.behavior: Upper-left saucer retains the ball on switch19 until public8 with lamp34=1 kicks it to play. The script uses InitSaucer sw19,19,155,8; angle155 and speed8 are table tuning, not factory geometry or physical timing. Shared public-driver ownership is recorded once under mechanism.expander; the exact selected loads are stated here and in its relay relationships.
mechanisms.label: Neptune's Cove Saucer

mechanisms.behavior: Four mechanically latching targets A(top) through D(bottom), switches4 through1. Public2 with lamp34=0 raises the bank. Targets remain down until reset; their make contacts follow target state. Completing all four collects Colossus, adds extended-play units and stops the right like-number digit. Shared public-driver ownership is recorded once under mechanism.expander; the exact selected loads are stated here and in its relay relationships.
mechanisms.label: Right Four Drop Target Bank

mechanisms.behavior: Seven targets ordered left-to-right48..42. Public3 lamp34=0 resets the bank; individual knockdowns are target1=public3 gated,2=public4 ungated,3=public4 gated,4=public5 ungated,5=public5 gated,6=public6 ungated,7=public6 gated. Preserve target memory and ROM-directed knockdown; a plain reset-only bank loses the feature. Held contacts must be released when the physical reset succeeds, otherwise the ROM retries. The generic parts drawing illustrates a four-target memory unit; it does not prove the coil count of this seven-target variant. Shared public-driver ownership is recorded once under mechanism.expander; the exact selected loads are stated here and in its relay relationships.
mechanisms.label: Seven Olympus Memory Drop Targets

mechanisms.behavior: The two upper flippers rotate normally and translate inward/outward as one latched linkage. Public1 with lamp34=1 opens the linkage; public2 gated closes it. Switch41 closes at the open position. The retained script substitutes alternate flipper objects and writes41 itself; that is a routing model, not two extra fitted flippers. Top target hits close the zipper. It reopens on timer expiry or when the ball leaves the upper area. DIP8 chooses accumulated10-second extensions versus a reset10-second interval. The parts drawing separately identifies the NB-24-1500 reset coil, GT-30-1300 latch coil, springs/linkage and both flipper assemblies; do not confuse winding EOS switches with matrix41. Shared public-driver ownership is recorded once under mechanism.expander; the exact selected loads are stated here and in its relay relationships.
mechanisms.label: Time Locked Zipper Flippers

mechanisms.behavior: Cabinet action button17 requests the ROM-controlled post pulse7. A rubbered post between the lower flippers returns a ball toward play. It starts with five credits, lane shots add credits, unused credits score10000 each at bonus. The table models its impulse with a plunger and two alternate walls; those are one mechanism, not three physical posts. Post returns when drive releases; do not hold the table impulse from a button directly.
mechanisms.label: Shield of the Gods Post

mechanisms.behavior: K1 enables four physical dual-winding flipper coils, two per cabinet button. Upper flippers are part of the zipper. Public45/46 and47/48 are synthetic pairs, not independent power/hold observations. Physical winding EOS contacts and lower-flipper illumination contacts are documented in the wiring and zipper assembly, separate from matrix41.
mechanisms.label: Four Cabinet-Wired Flippers

mechanisms.behavior: ROM causality confirmed separately:37->12,38->11,39->10,40->9,34->15,35->14,36->13. Each switch is stimulated separately in the retained gameplay trace. Physical locations follow Figure V; the table's first, second and fourth bumper handlers are rotated against those labels.
mechanisms.label: Four Bumpers and Three Slingshots

mechanisms.behavior: Lamp34 drives the expander optocoupler/relay and its internal indicator. Relay contacts select alternative loads for public1..6 and8. Use the lamp state at the output transition, as the retained script does. There is no public solenoid25..32 bank. The board is not a playfield lamp circuit merely because its gate uses the lamp callback.
mechanisms.label: AS-2518-66 Solenoid Expander

mechanisms.behavior: Own-game playfield schematic supplies general illumination from5.9VAC A2J1-4 (10) and -1 (70), with returns A2J1-6 (40) and -3 (50). Upper-flipper NC contacts switch the translucent lower-flipper lighting. PinMAME exposes no independent GI group for this driver. The script's29 GI objects and8 flipperlight helpers are a visual approximation; they do not establish sockets, quantities or string membership. A physical socket/harness survey remains required.
mechanisms.label: General Illumination and Flipper Lamps
